title.en: Framing and error control: find a frame, spot an error, even fix it
title.zh: 成帧与差错控制：找到一帧，发现错误，甚至改回来

description.en: Work out how the receiver finds frame boundaries in a long string of bits, and how redundancy lets it detect or even correct flipped bits; learn to compute parity, checksum, CRC and Hamming code.
description.zh: 弄清接收方怎样在一长串比特里找到帧的边界，又怎样靠冗余发现甚至改正翻转的比特，并会算奇偶、校验和、CRC 与汉明码。

name.zh: 成帧与字符计数 (framing, character count)
标志字节与字节填充 (flag bytes, byte stuffing)
起止标志与比特填充 (start/end flags, bit stuffing)

name.en: Error control: error types and the idea of detection vs correction
name.zh: 差错控制:错误类型与检错/纠错思路 (error control, detection vs correction)

name.en: Hamming distance and the limits of detection and correction
name.zh: 汉明距离与检错纠错的界限 (Hamming distance, error bounds)
循环冗余校验 (cyclic redundancy check, CRC)

name.en: Comparing error-detecting codes and choosing detection vs correction
name.zh: 检错码的比较与检错/纠错怎么选 (comparing codes, detection vs correction)
数据链路层与成帧 (data link layer, framing)
差错控制与汉明距离 (error control, Hamming distance)

description.en: Thinking a wrong character count only ruins one frame; in fact once a count is wrong, the boundary of every later frame is lost too.
description.zh: 以为字符计数出错只会坏一帧；其实计数一错，后面每一帧的边界都跟着丢。

description.en: Thinking bit stuffing adds a 0 only when the data “looks like a flag”; the rule is that a 0 always goes after five 1s.
description.zh: 以为比特填充只在数据「看起来像标志」时才补 0；规则是五个 1 后面一律补 0。

description.en: Mixing up framing (finding boundaries) with error control (detecting errors).
description.zh: 把成帧 (找边界) 和差错控制 (发现错误) 混为一谈。

description.en: Thinking an ESC in the data needs no escaping, or that the receiver simply deletes every ESC; the rule is that an ESC pairs with the one byte after it.
description.zh: 以为数据里的 ESC 不用转义，或者接收方把所有 ESC 一股脑删掉；规则是一个 ESC 配它后面的那一个字节。

description.en: Thinking the burst length is the number of flipped bits; it is the span from the first to the last bit in error.
description.zh: 以为突发长度就是被翻转的位数；它是第一个到最后一个出错位的跨度。

description.en: Thinking a parity check detects any error; it cannot detect an even number of bits wrong at once.
description.zh: 以为奇偶校验能发现任何错误；偶数个比特同时出错它检不出。

description.en: Thinking one code can push both detection and correction to the maximum.
description.zh: 以为同一个码可以同时把检错和纠错都开到最大。

description.en: Thinking a Hamming code can correct two wrong bits; it guarantees only one, and with two wrong bits it “corrects” to something wrong.
description.zh: 以为汉明码能纠两位错；它只保证纠一位，两位错会被改成错的。

description.en: Leaving out adding the carry back, or leaving out the ones' complement, when computing the Internet checksum.
description.zh: 算互联网校验和时漏掉进位加回，或漏掉取反码。

description.en: Thinking CRC just appends a few 0s to the frame, forgetting to fill in the remainder of the division.
description.zh: 以为 CRC 只是在帧后面补几个 0，忘了把除法的余数填进去。

description.en: Thinking that whenever a bit flips the CRC remainder is certainly not 0; when the error pattern happens to be a multiple of G, CRC cannot detect it either.
description.zh: 以为只要有比特被翻转，CRC 的余数就一定不是 0；错误图案恰好是 G 的倍数时，CRC 也检不出。

chapter.en: Finding the edge of a frame

title.en: One bit of the count goes wrong

prompt.en: The physical layer hands the receiver one long stream of bits with no separators. The most direct approach: put a number at the start of each frame saying how many bytes it holds. Now the 5 at the start of frame 2 is flipped by noise into a 7; everything else is fine. What does the receiver do?
prompt.zh: 物理层交给接收方的，是一长串没有任何分隔的比特。一种最直接的办法：每帧开头放一个数，写明这一帧有几个字节。现在，第二帧开头的 5 被噪声翻成了 7，其余都正常。接收方会怎样？

label.en: Only frame 2 is misread; later frames carry on as normal
label.zh: 只有第二帧读错，后面的帧照常

feedback.en: Frame 2 will take two extra bytes, so the count of the next frame is misread too. The boundary of every later frame is lost.
feedback.zh: 第二帧会多读两个字节，下一帧的计数就被读岔了。后面每一帧的边界都跟着丢。

label.en: Frame 2 is misread, and the boundaries of every later frame are scrambled too
label.zh: 第二帧读错，而且后面所有帧的边界都跟着乱

label.en: The receiver sees the number is wrong and corrects it back to 5
label.zh: 接收方发现数不对，自己改回 5

feedback.en: The count has no check of its own; the receiver cannot tell whether it is right.
feedback.zh: 计数本身没有任何检查，接收方不知道它对不对。

label.en: The link drops and has to be set up again

feedback.en: The wire is not down, only the boundaries are scrambled.
feedback.zh: 线并没有断，只是边界乱了。

explain.en: Right. Once a count is wrong, the error carries on down the line. Next, the details of this method and how to make it more robust.
explain.zh: 对。计数一错，错误就一路传下去。下面看这个办法的细节，以及怎样做得更稳。

title.en: Framing: find the boundaries first, then worry about correctness
title.zh: 成帧：先找到边界，再谈对错

text.en: To check for errors, or to hand a packet to the network layer, the receiver first has to know **where a frame starts and where it ends**. The bit stream arriving from the physical layer has no markers, so the link layer must cut it into frames itself. This is called framing.
text.zh: 接收方要检查错误，要把分组交给网络层，都得先知道 **一帧从哪里开始、到哪里结束**。物理层送来的比特流上没有任何标记，所以链路层要自己把它切成一个个帧。这叫成帧 (framing)。

body.en: The slides describe framing as “providing reliability” and use a checksum as an example. In fact framing only finds boundaries; whether bits have flipped is the job of error control, in the second half of this lesson. You have to find the frame before you can check it.
body.zh: 课件把成帧说成「提供可靠性」，还用校验和做例子。其实成帧只管找边界；比特有没有翻转，是后半课的差错控制。先找到帧，才谈得上检查它。

text.en: Three methods: character count, flag bytes with byte stuffing, and start and end flags with bit stuffing. Start with the most direct one, character count: put a field at the head of the frame saying how many characters (bytes) the frame has.
text.zh: 三种办法：字符计数 (character count)、带字节填充的标志字节 (flag bytes)、带比特填充的起止标志 (start and end flags)。先看最直接的：字符计数，在帧头放一个字段，写明这一帧有几个字符 (字节)。

alt.zh: 上：四个帧的计数分别是 5、5、8、8，边界清楚。下：第二帧的计数被翻成 7，多读了两个字节，后面的数据字节被当成计数，边界全乱

caption.en: Count bytes are in bold red.

text.en: With no errors, the receiver reads the count, counts off that many bytes, and the next byte is a new count. Simple and compact. But once a count is corrupted by noise, the receiver reads too much or too little, and the next “count” is really a data byte; every later frame is misaligned, and nothing in the data gives a mark to realign on.
text.zh: 没有错误时，接收方读到计数，就数出这么多字节，下一个字节又是新的计数。简单、省空间。可是一旦某个计数被噪声弄坏，接收方就读多或读少，下一个「计数」其实是数据字节；后面的帧全部错位，而且数据里没有任何记号可供重新对齐。

text.en: So real data link protocols mostly combine character count with another method: the count reads frames quickly, and the other kind of marker finds the boundary again after an error.
text.zh: 所以实际的数据链路协议多半把字符计数和另一种办法结合起来：计数用来快速读帧，另一种记号用来在出错后重新找到边界。

text.en: Change the approach: instead of counting, put in markers. Each frame begins and ends with a special **flag byte**, FLAG. The receiver reads along, and whenever it sees a FLAG it knows a boundary. Errors are no problem: look ahead for the next FLAG to realign.
text.zh: 换个思路：不数，做记号。每一帧以一个特殊的 **标志字节** FLAG 开头和结尾。接收方一路读，见到 FLAG 就知道边界。出错了也不怕，往后找下一个 FLAG 就能重新对齐。

alt.en: Top: a frame is FLAG, header, payload, trailer, FLAG in turn. Bottom: when the payload A FLAG B is sent, an extra ESC goes in front of the FLAG, giving A ESC FLAG B
alt.zh: 上：一个帧依次是 FLAG、头部、载荷、尾部、FLAG。下：载荷 A FLAG B 发出去时，在 FLAG 前面多了一个 ESC，变成 A ESC FLAG B

caption.en: A FLAG at each end of the frame; a FLAG in the payload gets an ESC in front.
caption.zh: 帧的两头各有一个 FLAG；载荷里的 FLAG 前面要加 ESC。

text.en: The trouble: a byte in the payload happens to equal FLAG, and the receiver thinks the frame ends there. The fix is **byte stuffing**. First agree on an escape byte ESC. There is only one rule:
text.zh: 麻烦在于：载荷里碰巧有一个字节和 FLAG 一样，接收方会以为帧到此结束。办法是 **字节填充** (byte stuffing)。先约定一个转义字节 ESC，规则只有一条：

body.en: Sender: every FLAG or ESC in the payload gets an ESC inserted in front of it. Receiver: every time it sees an ESC, it deletes it and treats the next byte as ordinary data, whatever it is.
body.zh: 发送方：载荷里每遇到一个 FLAG 或 ESC，就在它前面插一个 ESC。接收方：每见到一个 ESC，就把它删掉，并把后面那一个字节当成普通数据，不管它是什么。

rows.en: ESC deleted, FLAG treated as data
rows.zh: ESC 删掉，FLAG 当成数据

rows.en: The first ESC is deleted, the second ESC treated as data
rows.zh: 第一个 ESC 删掉，第二个 ESC 当成数据

rows: A ESC ESC ESC FLAG B

rows.en: ESC ESC restores to one ESC, ESC FLAG restores to FLAG
rows.zh: ESC ESC 还原成一个 ESC，ESC FLAG 还原成 FLAG

rows: A ESC ESC ESC ESC B

rows.en: Each ESC pairs with one ESC, restoring two ESCs
rows.zh: 每个 ESC 各配一个 ESC，还原成两个 ESC

text.en: Why must ESC itself be escaped? If it isn't, an ESC already in the data would be taken by the receiver as an escape marker and swallow the next byte, quietly altering the original data.
text.zh: 为什么 ESC 自己也要转义？如果不转义，数据里本来就有的 ESC 会被接收方当成转义记号，吃掉后面一个字节，原数据就被悄悄改了。

prompt.en: A link uses byte stuffing. Between two FLAGs the receiver reads A ESC ESC ESC FLAG B. Which payload did the sender originally want to send?
prompt.zh: 一条链路用字节填充。接收方在两个 FLAG 之间读到 A ESC ESC ESC FLAG B。发送方原来要送的载荷是哪一个？

feedback.en: This deletes every ESC. The rule is that an ESC pairs with the one byte after it: ESC ESC restores to one ESC, and ESC FLAG restores to FLAG.
feedback.zh: 这是把所有 ESC 都删掉了。规则是一个 ESC 配它后面的那一个字节：ESC ESC 还原成一个 ESC，ESC FLAG 还原成 FLAG。

feedback.en: Only one ESC was deleted. Read the three ESCs as pairs: the first ESC takes the second ESC along, the third ESC takes FLAG along, and in each pair the front one is deleted.
feedback.zh: 只删了一个 ESC。三个 ESC 要两两看：第一个 ESC 带着第二个 ESC，第三个 ESC 带着 FLAG，各自删掉前面那一个。

label.en: A ESC ESC ESC FLAG B, unchanged
label.zh: A ESC ESC ESC FLAG B，原样不变

feedback.en: This is what is on the wire, not the payload. The stuffing was added by the sender; the receiver has to delete the ESCs that were added.
feedback.zh: 这是线上的样子，不是载荷。填充是发送方加的，接收方要把加的 ESC 删掉。

explain.en: Read left to right: A is an ordinary byte; the first ESC is deleted and the ESC after it is treated as data; the third ESC is deleted and the FLAG after it is treated as data; last comes B. So the payload is A ESC FLAG B. Now think about why ESC itself must be escaped: if only FLAG were escaped, this payload would be sent as A ESC ESC FLAG B, and once the receiver treats the second ESC as data, the next FLAG would be taken as the end of the frame, cutting the frame short.
explain.zh: 从左往右读：A 是普通字节；第一个 ESC 被删掉，它后面的 ESC 当成数据；第三个 ESC 被删掉，它后面的 FLAG 当成数据；最后是 B。所以载荷是 A ESC FLAG B。再想一想为什么 ESC 自己也要转义：假如只转义 FLAG，这个载荷会被发成 A ESC ESC FLAG B，接收方把第二个 ESC 当成数据之后，下一个 FLAG 就被当成帧的结束，帧被提前截断。

text.en: Byte stuffing requires frames to be a whole number of bytes. Another method works at the bit level: each frame begins and ends with the special bit pattern `01111110`. The advantage is that a frame can contain any number of bits.
text.zh: 字节填充要求帧是整数个字节。另一种办法在比特层做：每帧以特殊的比特模式 `01111110` 开头和结尾。好处是帧可以含任意个比特。

text.en: What if `01111110` shows up in the data? The rule of **bit stuffing**:
text.zh: 数据里碰巧出现 `01111110` 怎么办？**比特填充** (bit stuffing) 的规则：

body.en: Sender: whenever five consecutive 1s appear in the data, insert a 0 after them, whatever would have come next. Receiver: whenever it sees five consecutive 1s, delete the 0 after them (destuffing).
body.zh: 发送方：数据里每出现连续五个 1，就在后面补一个 0，不管后面原本是什么。接收方：每见到连续五个 1，就把它后面的那个 0 删掉 (destuffing)。

text.en: Why five? The flag has six consecutive 1s. Stuffing guarantees the data never contains six consecutive 1s, so whenever six 1s are seen it must be a flag.
text.zh: 为什么是五个？标志里有连续六个 1。填充保证数据里永远不会出现六个连续的 1，所以只要看到六个 1，就一定是标志。

caption.en: 12 consecutive 1s: a 0 goes after each group of five, and the remaining two 1s need none. The receiver deletes the 0 after each five 1s and recovers the original.
caption.zh: 12 个连续的 1：每五个后面补一个 0，剩下的两个 1 不用补。接收方删掉五个 1 后面的 0，就还原了。

prompt.en: Send the data 1111101111110 using bit stuffing. Which bit string goes out after stuffing?
prompt.zh: 用比特填充发送数据 1111101111110。填充后发出的比特串是哪一个？

label.en: 1111101111110, it already has a 0, so no stuffing is needed

feedback.en: The rule is that a 0 always goes after five 1s, regardless of what was there before.
feedback.zh: 规则是五个 1 后面一律补 0，不看后面原本是什么。

label.en: 11111001111110, stuffing just one at the start

feedback.en: The middle part has six consecutive 1s; a 0 goes after the first five of those as well.
feedback.zh: 中间那段有六个连续的 1，前五个后面也要补 0。

explain.en: The data is 11111 0 111111 0: five 1s, a 0, six 1s, a 0. Write the inserted 0s as [0]: after the first five 1s insert [0], and the data's own 0 follows right after, giving 11111[0]0; in the middle six 1s, a [0] goes after the first five, while the sixth 1 and the final data 0 stay as they are, giving 11111[0]10. Together that is 11111[0]0 11111[0]10, that is, 111110011111010. The slides' exercise works the same way: in 0111110111 a 0 must go after the five 1s even if a 0 was already there, giving 01111100111.
explain.zh: 数据是 11111 0 111111 0：五个 1，一个 0，六个 1，一个 0。把插入的 0 记作 [0]：第一组五个 1 后面插入 [0]，数据自己的 0 紧跟在后面，得 11111[0]0；中间六个 1 里，前五个后面插入 [0]，第六个 1 和最后数据自己的 0 照旧，得 11111[0]10。合起来是 11111[0]0 11111[0]10，也就是 111110011111010。课件那道题同理：0111110111 里五个 1 后面必须补 0，哪怕后面原本就是 0，变成 01111100111。

title.en: Bits flip: one, or a run of them
title.zh: 比特会翻转：一位，还是一串

text.en: The boundaries are found; the next question: have any bits in this frame flipped? Physical media make errors, which may appear at random or in runs.
text.zh: 边界找到了，下一个问题：这一帧里有没有比特被翻转？物理介质会出错，可能随机地出现，也可能成串地出现。

items.zh: **单比特错误** (single-bit error)：只有一位变了。

items.en: **Burst error**: two or more bits changed. The burst length is the span from the first bit in error to the last, counting the correct bits in between. In the slides' example the length is 8, with 4 bits corrupted.
items.zh: **突发错误** (burst error)：两个或更多比特变了。突发长度是从第一个出错比特到最后一个出错比特的跨度，中间没出错的也算在内。课件的例子里长度是 8，其中 4 位被破坏。

text.en: Why do errors come in runs? Noise often lasts a short while: a burst of electromagnetic interference, a flash of lightning, a loose contact. The faster the line, the more bits are destroyed in the same stretch of time.
text.zh: 错误为什么会成串？噪声往往持续一小段时间：一次电磁干扰、一阵闪电、一下接触不良。线路速度越高，同样一段时间里被毁掉的比特越多。

text.en: The slides say burst errors are easier to detect but harder to repair. “Easier to detect” holds for stronger codes: when a whole stretch of bits is scrambled, a CRC is guaranteed to catch every burst no longer than its number of check bits. But that does not mean every detection method does well: a one-bit parity check only looks at whether the number of 1s is odd or even, and if an even number of bits break it sees nothing (more on this later). “Harder to repair” is because the broken bits form a block, and fixing them takes much more redundancy.
text.zh: 课件说突发错误更容易检出，但更难修复。更容易检出，是对强一点的码说的：一大段比特都乱了，CRC 保证抓住所有长度不超过它校验位数的突发。但这不等于每种检错办法都行：一位的奇偶校验只看 1 的个数是奇是偶，坏了偶数位它就看不见 (后面会看到)。更难修复，是因为坏的位连成一片，要改回来，需要的冗余多得多。

prompt.en: 011001011010 is sent and 010101010010 is received. This is a burst error. What is its burst length?
prompt.zh: 发送 011001011010，收到 010101010010。这是一次突发错误，它的突发长度是多少？

feedback.en: 3 is the number of flipped bits. Burst length is the span, and the unbroken bits in between count too.
feedback.zh: 3 是被翻转的位数。突发长度算的是跨度，中间没坏的位也算在内。

feedback.en: 9 − 3 = 6 undercounts by one: counting from bit 3 to bit 9 includes both ends, 7 bits in all.
feedback.zh: 9 − 3 = 6 少算了一位：从第 3 位数到第 9 位，两头都要算，一共 7 位。

feedback.en: The length is counted from the first bit in error, not from the start of the frame.
feedback.zh: 长度从第一个出错位开始数，不是从帧的开头数。

explain.en: Compare the two strings: only bits 3, 4 and 9 differ. From the first bit in error (bit 3) to the last (bit 9) is 7 bits, of which 3 are actually broken. The slides' example is the same: length 8, 4 broken.
explain.zh: 对照两串：只有第 3、4、9 位不同。从第一个出错位 (第 3 位) 到最后一个 (第 9 位)，一共 7 位，其中真正坏了的是 3 位。课件的例子同理：长度 8，坏了 4 位。

title.en: Two paths: detect and resend, or fix it directly
title.zh: 两条路：检出后重发，或者直接改回来

text.en: There is only one way to fight errors: **add redundancy**. The sender computes a few extra check bits from the data and sends them along; the receiver recomputes and compares. The goal is that a corrupted message is never mistaken for the original.
text.zh: 对付错误只有一个办法：**加冗余**。发送方按数据算出几个额外的校验位 (check bits)，随数据一起发；接收方重算、对照。目的是让被损坏的消息，不会被当成原消息。

items.en: **Detect and retransmit**: if something is wrong, throw the frame away and have the sender send it again. This is the acknowledgement and resend of the previous lesson.
items.zh: **检错后重传** (detect and retransmit)：发现不对就丢掉，让发送方再发。这就是上一课的确认与重发。

items.en: **Correct**: there are enough check bits to point out which bits are wrong, and the receiver fixes them itself, with no resend.
items.zh: **纠错** (correct)：校验位多到足以指出是哪些位错了，接收方自己改回来，不用重发。

text.en: Both paths must finish before the data goes to the network layer; the mechanism should be fast (low computation cost), and the extra bits few.
text.zh: 两条路都要在把数据交给网络层之前做完；机制要快 (计算开销低)，额外的比特要少。

title.zh: 超出课件：那张 001 → 111 → 001 的图

body.en: The small figure on slide 18 is only a sketch, not any particular code. Later we will work out that to restore a string with two bits wrong, the code's Hamming distance must be at least 5, which a code with only 000 and 111 cannot do.
body.zh: 课件第 18 页的小图只是示意，不是哪个具体的码。后面会算到：要把错两位的串改回来，码的汉明距离至少要 5，一个只有 000 和 111 的码做不到。

prompt.en: The crudest redundancy: send each bit three times, 0 as 000 and 1 as 111, and the receiver takes a majority vote. A 0 (that is, 000) is sent, two bits flip on the way, and 110 arrives. What does the receiver conclude?
prompt.zh: 最笨的冗余：每个比特发三遍，0 发 000，1 发 111，接收方多数表决。发送的是 0 (即 000)，路上有两位被翻转，收到 110。接收方会得出什么？

label.en: 0, corrected right

feedback.en: In 110 the 1s are the majority, so the vote gives 1.
feedback.zh: 110 里 1 占多数，表决的结果是 1。

label.en: 1, corrected wrongly
1, and it is right

feedback.en: A 0 was sent, so 1 is wrong.
feedback.zh: 发的是 0，所以 1 是错的。

label.en: It knows an error occurred but not what the original was
label.zh: 知道出了错，但不知道原来是什么

feedback.en: A majority vote always gives an answer; it does not know it is wrong.
feedback.zh: 多数表决总会给出一个答案，它不知道自己错了。

explain.en: A majority vote can only withstand one error; two fool it. Next, “Hamming distance” makes this limit exact.
explain.zh: 多数表决只能扛住一位错误，两位就被骗了。下面用「汉明距离」把这个界限算清楚。

title.en: Think of valid codewords as points

text.en: A **code** turns n data bits into an n+k bit **codeword**. There are many strings of n+k bits, and only a small part of them are valid codewords. When the receiver gets an invalid string, it knows an error occurred. In the repeat-three-times code the only valid ones are 000 and 111.
text.zh: 一个 **码** (code) 把 n 位数据变成 n+k 位的 **码字** (codeword)。n+k 位的串有很多，只有一小部分是合法码字。接收方收到不合法的串，就知道出错了。重复三遍的码里，合法的只有 000 和 111。

text.en: **Hamming distance**: the minimum number of bits that must flip to turn one valid codeword into another. The distance of the whole code is the smallest over all pairs of valid codewords. The distance between 000 and 111 is 3.
text.zh: **汉明距离** (Hamming distance)：把一个合法码字变成另一个合法码字，至少要翻转多少个比特。整个码的距离，取所有合法码字对里最小的那个。000 和 111 的距离是 3。

text.en: The slides have a second code: 2 data bits, each repeated 5 times, becoming a 10-bit codeword (n=2, k=8). The examples below all use it.
text.zh: 课件还有第二个码：2 位数据，每一位重复 5 遍，变成 10 位的码字 (n=2，k=8)。后面的例子都用它。

text.en: Any two codewords differ in at least 5 bits, so the distance of this code is 5. The figure below treats codewords as points on a line: A is the codeword for 00, 00000 00000, and B is the codeword for 10, 11111 00000.
text.zh: 任意两个码字至少差 5 位，所以这个码的距离是 5。下图把码字看成一条线上的点：A 是 00 的码字 00000 00000，B 是 10 的码字 11111 00000。

alt.en: Six points on a line. The left end is valid codeword A and the right end is valid codeword B; between them are the strings with 1 to 4 bits flipped. The three points nearer A are changed back to A, and the three nearer B are changed to B
alt.zh: 一条线上六个点，左端是合法码字 A，右端是合法码字 B，中间依次是翻转 1 到 4 位的串；离 A 近的三个点改回 A，离 B 近的三个点改成 B

caption.en: An error means being pushed some number of steps along.
caption.zh: 出错就是被推着走了几步。

title.en: Distance decides how much detection and correction a code can do
title.zh: 距离决定检错和纠错的本事

intro.en: One figure, two questions: how many errors can the code detect at most, and how many can it correct at most. The examples use the codewords of the 10-bit code above.
intro.zh: 同一张图，回答两个问题：最多能检出几位错，最多能纠正几位错。例子用上面 10 位码的码字。

lines.tex: \text{detect up to } d \text{ errors: distance} \ge d+1

why.en: Detection relies on “receiving an invalid codeword”. If no more than d bits flip, you cannot reach another valid codeword at distance d+1, so you must land on an invalid string. Flip d+1 bits and you may land exactly on another valid codeword, which goes undetected.
why.zh: 检错靠「收到非法码字」。翻转不超过 d 位，走不到相距 d+1 的另一个合法码字，落点一定是非法串。翻转 d+1 位，就可能正好走到另一个合法码字，检不出。

why.en: 00000 11111 is the codeword for data 01. Flip 1 bit and you get an invalid string: detected. Flip 5 bits and it becomes exactly the codeword for data 11: not detected.
why.zh: 00000 11111 是数据 01 的码字。翻 1 位，得到非法串，检出了；翻 5 位，正好变成数据 11 的码字，检不出。

why.en: Correction relies on “changing to the nearest valid codeword”. Draw a ball of radius d around each valid codeword; every string inside a ball is changed back to the centre. For the balls not to overlap, two centres must be at least 2d+1 apart.
why.zh: 纠错靠「改成离得最近的合法码字」。以每个合法码字为中心画半径 d 的球，落在球里的串都改回球心。要让球不相交，两个中心至少相距 2d+1。

why.en: It is 2 steps from 00000 00000 and 3 steps from 11111 00000; the nearest is still the original codeword, so it is corrected right.
why.zh: 它离 00000 00000 是 2 步，离 11111 00000 是 3 步，最近的仍是原来的码字，纠对了。

why.en: Now it is only 2 steps from 11111 00000, closer than to the original codeword (3 steps), so it is changed to the wrong one.
why.zh: 现在它离 11111 00000 只有 2 步，比离原码字 (3 步) 更近，被改成了错的。

outro.en: One code cannot push both to the maximum. A distance-3 code either corrects 1 bit or detects 2. If it is used for correction, a string with 2 bits wrong looks like another codeword with 1 bit wrong, and will be corrected wrongly.
outro.zh: 同一个码不能把两样都开到最大。距离 3 的码，要么纠 1 位，要么检 2 位。因为如果拿来纠错，错 2 位的串看起来就像另一个码字错了 1 位，会被改错。

prompt.en: A code has only two valid codewords: 0000000 and 1111111 (distance 7). 0000000 is sent, and the receiver changes whatever it receives to the nearest valid codeword. Which of these errors makes it get changed to the wrong one?
prompt.zh: 一个码只有两个合法码字：0000000 和 1111111 (距离 7)。发送的是 0000000，接收方把收到的串改成离它最近的合法码字。下面哪个错误，会让它被改成错的？

label.en: Receive 0000011 (2 bits wrong)

feedback.en: It is only 2 steps from 0000000 and 5 steps from 1111111, so it is corrected right.

label.en: Receive 0001110 (3 bits wrong)

feedback.en: It is 3 steps from 0000000 and 4 from 1111111, so it is still corrected right. Distance 7 = 2×3+1, exactly enough to correct 3 bits.

label.en: Receive 0011110 (4 bits wrong)
All of the above are corrected right

feedback.en: 4 wrong bits is already beyond the limit of 3; check which codeword it is nearer to.
feedback.zh: 错 4 位已经超过了 3 位的界限，要看它离哪个码字更近。

explain.en: Distance 7 = 2d+1 gives d = 3: at most 3 bits can be corrected. 0011110 is only 3 steps from 1111111, closer than to 0000000 (4 steps), so it is changed to 1111111, wrongly. If the same code were used only for detection, it could detect up to 6 bits.
explain.zh: 距离 7 = 2d+1 给出 d = 3：最多纠 3 位。0011110 离 1111111 只有 3 步，比离 0000000 (4 步) 更近，被改成 1111111，改错了。同一个码如果只做检错，最多能检出 6 位。

text.en: First define **overhead**: extra bits sent ÷ data bits.
text.zh: 先定义 **开销** (overhead)：额外发的比特数 ÷ 数据比特数。

rows.en: Repeat each bit three times, majority vote (0→000, 1→111)
rows.zh: 每位重复三遍，多数表决 (0→000，1→111)

rows.en: 2 bits wrong: the majority vote is wrong. 3 bits wrong: it becomes another valid codeword, undetected
rows.zh: 错 2 位：多数表决判错。错 3 位：变成另一个合法码字，检不出

rows.en: 2 data bits repeated into a 10-bit codeword (the table on the previous page)
rows.zh: 2 位数据重复成 10 位码字 (上一页的表)

rows.en: 3 bits wrong: correction changes it to the wrong one. 5 bits wrong: it may land on another valid codeword
rows.zh: 错 3 位：纠错会改成错的。错 5 位：可能撞上别的合法码字

text.en: In the second code, any two codewords differ in at least 5 bits. Use it to check the slides' two questions: 00000 00000 with 2 bits wrong becomes 11000 00000, whose nearest codeword is still 00000 00000, so it is corrected right; with 3 bits wrong it becomes 11100 00000, whose nearest is now 11111 00000, so it is corrected wrongly.
text.zh: 第二个码里，任意两个码字至少差 5 位。用它验证课件的两个问题：00000 00000 错 2 位变成 11000 00000，最近的仍是 00000 00000，纠对；错 3 位变成 11100 00000，最近的变成 11111 00000，纠错了。

body.en: The power is bought with overhead: every data bit is sent several times over. The codes that follow detect errors or correct one bit with far fewer extra bits.
body.zh: 本事靠开销换来，每个数据位都要多发好几位。后面的几种码，用少得多的额外位做到检错或纠一位。

title.en: Parity bit: one bit of redundancy
title.zh: 奇偶校验位：一个比特的冗余

text.en: The thriftiest redundancy: count the 1s in the data and add one bit so the total becomes even (**even parity**) or odd (**odd parity**). The data 10001110 has four 1s: even parity appends 0, giving 100011100; odd parity appends 1, giving 100011101. The receiver counts the 1s and reports an error if the count doesn't match.
text.zh: 最省的冗余：数一数据里有几个 1，补一位，让总数变成偶数 (**偶校验**，even parity) 或奇数 (**奇校验**，odd parity)。数据 10001110 有四个 1：偶校验补 0，得 100011100；奇校验补 1，得 100011101。接收方数一数 1 的个数，对不上就报错。

text.en: Why is the distance 2? Flipping any one bit changes the parity of the number of 1s, so a valid codeword with one bit flipped is always an invalid string; to reach another valid codeword takes at least two flips.
text.zh: 为什么距离是 2？翻转任意一位，都会改变 1 的个数的奇偶，所以一个合法码字翻一位，一定落到非法串；要到另一个合法码字，至少要翻两位。

text.en: A distance of 2 means it can detect 1-bit errors (d+1=2) but cannot correct. The receiver knows something is wrong but not which bit.
text.zh: 距离 2 意味着：能检出 1 位错 (d+1=2)，纠不了错。接收方知道有错，但不知道是哪一位。

body.en: When an even number of bits are wrong (2, 4, ...), the parity of the number of 1s does not change, so the error goes undetected. So against burst errors, a parity check often sees nothing.
body.zh: 偶数个比特同时出错 (2 位、4 位......)，1 的个数的奇偶不变，检不出。所以遇到突发错误，奇偶校验常常看不见。

title.en: Two bits wrong: can it see?

prompt.en: Even parity: the data 1011001 has four 1s, the check bit appended is 0, and the frame sent is 10110010. On the way bits 2 and 3 are flipped, and 11010010 is received. What does the receiver do?
prompt.zh: 偶校验：数据 1011001 有四个 1，校验位补 0，发出的帧是 10110010。路上第 2、3 位被翻转，收到 11010010。接收方会怎样？

label.en: Detects the error and asks for a resend

feedback.en: It only counts 1s: the received string still has four, an even number, the same as before, so it sees nothing.
feedback.zh: 它只数 1 的个数：收到的串里还是 4 个，偶数，和原来一样，所以看不出。

label.en: Passes it as normal; the error goes unnoticed
label.zh: 照常通过，错误没被发现

label.en: Detects the error and corrects the two bits
label.zh: 发现出错，并把错的两位改回来

feedback.en: Parity carries no information about location; it detects a one-bit error at most and can never correct. And here it does not even detect.
feedback.zh: 奇偶校验没有任何定位的信息，最多检出一位错，从来不能纠错；何况这里连检出都没有。

label.en: Detects the error but doesn't know which bits
label.zh: 发现出错，但不知道是哪几位

feedback.en: That is the result when 1 bit (or an odd number of bits) is wrong. Here two bits flipped, the number of 1s didn't change, and it reports nothing at all.
feedback.zh: 这是错 1 位 (或奇数位) 时的结果。这里翻了两位，1 的个数没变，它根本不报错。

explain.en: Bit 2 changes from 0 to 1, adding a 1; bit 3 changes from 1 to 0, removing a 1; the total is still 4, even, so the check passes. When an even number of bits are wrong, the parity of the number of 1s never changes, and a one-bit parity check cannot see it. To see this kind of error you need a stronger code.
explain.zh: 第 2 位 0 变成 1，多出一个 1；第 3 位 1 变成 0，少掉一个 1；总数仍是 4，偶数，校验通过。偶数个比特出错，1 的个数的奇偶都不变，一位的奇偶校验看不见。要看见这类错误，得用更强的码。

title.en: The Internet checksum: add the data up as numbers
title.zh: 互联网校验和：把数据当数相加

intro.en: One check bit is too weak. The idea of the Internet checksum: cut the data into words (16 bits in practice, 5 bits in the example below), add all the words to get a sum, and attach the ones' complement of that sum when sending. The receiver adds all the words plus the checksum again, and if nothing went wrong gets all 1s: a number plus its complement is 1 in every bit. The algorithm has two details: the carry must be added back into the low bit, or the information in the top bit is lost; and what is attached is the complement of the sum (every bit inverted), not the sum itself.
intro.zh: 一位校验太弱。互联网校验和的想法：把数据切成一段一段的字 (真实用 16 位，下面的例子用 5 位)，把所有字加起来得到一个和，发送时附上这个和的反码。这样接收方把所有字连同校验和再加一遍，没出错就应该得到全 1：一个数加上它的反码，每一位都是 1。算法有两个细节：进位要加回低位，不然最高位的信息会丢；附上的是和的反码 (每位取反)，不是和本身。

why.en: Adding the first two words: 6 + 17 = 23.
why.zh: 前两个字相加：6 + 17 = 23。

why.en: The result goes beyond 5 bits, so the carry 1 out of the top bit is added back into the lowest bit.
why.zh: 结果超出 5 位，最高位的进位 1 加回最低位。

why.en: Adding the fourth word, the total is 11100.
why.zh: 加第四个字，总和是 11100。

why.en: Take the ones' complement to get the checksum 00011. Sent: 00110 10001 11001 01011 00011.

Receiver's check: add up all the words with the checksum (again adding the carry back), and if the result is all 1s it passes. Because a number plus its complement is exactly 1 in every bit; if any bit is flipped, the result is usually no longer all 1s.
why.zh: 接收方验证：把所有字连同校验和加起来 (同样把进位加回)，得到全 1 就通过。因为一个数加上它的反码，正好每位都是 1；只要有位被翻转，通常就不再是全 1。

outro.en: Weakness: addition is commutative, so swapping two words leaves the sum unchanged and the checksum still passes: the error goes undetected. Its Hamming distance is 2.
outro.zh: 弱点：加法交换，调换两个字的顺序，总和不变，校验和照样通过，检不出。它的汉明距离是 2。

prompt.en: Compute the Internet checksum with 5-bit words; the data is 01001 10110 00111. What is the checksum?
prompt.zh: 用 5 位字算互联网校验和，数据是 01001 10110 00111。校验和是多少？

feedback.en: This is the sum after adding the carry back; the complement has not been taken yet.
feedback.zh: 这是进位加回后的和，还没有取反码。

feedback.en: The last addition gives 100110, which goes beyond 5 bits; the carry 1 must be added back into the low bit, and then complemented. Leaving out the carry gives this answer.
feedback.zh: 最后一步加得到 100110，超出了 5 位，进位 1 要加回低位，再取反。漏掉进位就得到这个。

explain.en: 01001 + 10110 = 11111; adding 00111 gives 100110, beyond 5 bits, so add the carry back: 00110 + 1 = 00111; the ones' complement is 11000. Receiver's check: 01001 + 10110 = 11111; adding 00111 gives 100110, and the carry added back makes 00111; adding the checksum 11000 gives 11111, all 1s, so it passes.

title.en: CRC: use a remainder to make the number divisible
title.zh: CRC：用余数把数补成能整除

text.en: The checksum has a blind spot: swap two words and the sum is unchanged, so nothing is found. A cyclic redundancy check (CRC) is sensitive to position too, and is cheap to build in hardware. Its core is a trick from primary-school arithmetic: use the remainder to make a number divisible.
text.zh: 校验和有个盲点：调换两个字的顺序，和不变，查不出。循环冗余校验 (cyclic redundancy check, CRC) 对位置也敏感，硬件做起来又便宜。它的核心是一个小学算术里的把戏：用余数把一个数补成能整除。

text.en: 1000 divided by 7 leaves 6; subtract the remainder and the 994 that remains is divisible by 7. The receiver asks only one thing: is the number received divisible by 7? If 994 turns into 995 on the way, dividing by 7 leaves 1 and the error shows at once.
text.zh: 1000 除以 7 余 6，把余数减掉，剩下的 994 就能被 7 整除。接收方只问一件事：收到的数能不能被 7 整除？路上 994 变成了 995，除以 7 余 1，立刻露馅。

text.en: CRC moves this trick onto bit strings: the sender pads the frame into a bit string divisible by an agreed G, and the receiver divides once; a remainder of 0 means pass. Two things have to change:
text.zh: CRC 把这个把戏搬到比特串上：发送方把帧补成一个能被事先约定好的 G 整除的比特串，接收方除一遍，余数是 0 就通过。要换两样东西：

items.en: **Bit strings as polynomials**. 1101001 is $x^6+x^5+x^3+1$, each bit being the coefficient of one term. G is written the same way and is called the **generator polynomial**, for example $G(x)=x^4+x+1$, the bit string 10011, with highest degree $r=4$.
items.zh: **比特串当多项式**。1101001 就是 $x^6+x^5+x^3+1$，每一位是一项的系数。G 也这样写，叫 **生成多项式** (generator polynomial)，例如 $G(x)=x^4+x+1$，比特串 10011，最高次数 $r=4$。

items.en: **Arithmetic becomes modulo 2**. No carries and no borrows; addition and subtraction both equal exclusive-or (XOR): 0⊕0=0, 1⊕1=0, 0⊕1=1. The benefit is that “subtract the remainder” and “add the remainder” are the same thing, and hardware can do it with a shift register and XOR gates.
items.zh: **算术换成模 2**。没有进位，也没有借位，加和减都等于异或 (XOR)：0⊕0=0，1⊕1=0，0⊕1=1。好处是「减去余数」和「加上余数」是同一件事，硬件用移位寄存器和异或门就能做。

text.en: The sender's four steps (the slides' steps):
text.zh: 发送方四步 (课件的步骤)：

items.en: Append r 0s at the low end of the frame, leaving room for the remainder. 1101001 with 0000 appended gives 11010010000.
Divide it by G using modulo-2 division to get the remainder (at most r bits).
items.zh: 用 G 对它做模 2 除法，得到余数 (最多 r 位)。

items.en: Fill the remainder into the positions of the appended 0s; this is the 1000 − 6 step.
items.zh: 把余数填进补的那几个 0 的位置，就是 1000 − 6 的那一步。

items.en: The frame T obtained this way is divisible by G; send it out.
items.zh: 这样得到的帧 T 能被 G 整除，把它发出去。

title.en: Modulo-2 long division: the CRC of 1101001
title.zh: 模 2 长除法：算 1101001 的 CRC

text.en: Like ordinary long division, except that each subtraction is an XOR, and the quotient isn't needed. At each step look at the top bit of the current 5 bits: if it is 1, XOR with G (10011); if it is 0, XOR with 00000, that is, don't subtract; then drop the leading 0s and bring down the next bit from the dividend.
text.zh: 和平时的长除法一样，只是每一步的减是异或，而且商用不着。每一步看当前 5 位的最高位：是 1 就异或 G (10011)，是 0 就异或 00000，也就是不减；然后去掉前导的 0，从被除数里拉下一位。

caption.en: Each row is aligned at the digit position it works on.
caption.zh: 每一行都对齐在它所在的数位上。

text.en: The remainder is 0101. Fill it into the appended 0000 and the frame sent is 11010010101. (The slides' box shows 00101; that is the five-bit difference of the last step, and the remainder takes only the low r = 4 bits.)
text.zh: 余数是 0101。把它填进补的 0000，发出的帧是 11010010101。(课件的框里写 00101，那是最后一次的五位差，余数只取低 r = 4 位。)

text.en: Receiver: divide the whole received string 11010010101 by G the same way; a remainder of 0 means pass.
text.zh: 接收方：把收到的整串 11010010101 对 G 做同样的除法，余数为 0 就通过。

summary.zh: 接收方的除法，对照着看

prompt.en: The data is 1010, and the generator polynomial is $G(x)=x^4+x+1$ (bit string 10011). Which frame is sent?
prompt.zh: 数据是 1010，生成多项式 $G(x)=x^4+x+1$ (比特串 10011)。要发送的帧是哪一个？

feedback.en: This only appended 4 0s; the remainder has not been filled in. A string padded with 0s is generally not divisible by G, so the receiver's division will fail.
feedback.zh: 这只是补了 4 个 0，还没有把余数填进去。补 0 的串一般不能被 G 整除，接收方一除就不通过。

feedback.en: The remainder is 1101, and here it was written backwards as 1011. The remainder goes into the low 4 bits in its original order.
feedback.zh: 余数是 1101，这里写成了反过来的 1011。余数要按原来的次序填进低 4 位。

feedback.en: The remainder was put in front of the data. It goes into the positions of the appended 0s, that is, at the end of the frame.
feedback.zh: 余数填到了数据前面。它要填进补 0 的位置，也就是帧的末尾。

hints.en: First append 4 0s to get 10100000, then divide by 10011.
At a step where the top bit is 0, don't subtract.
hints.zh: 最高位是 0 的那一步，不减。

explain.en: Appending 4 0s gives 10100000. The first 5 bits 10100 have top bit 1; XOR with 10011 gives 00111, bring down a 0 to get 01110; the top bit is 0, so don't subtract, bring down a 0 to get 11100; XOR with 10011 gives 01111, bring down the last 0 to get 11110; XOR with 10011 again gives 01101. The remainder is the low 4 bits, 1101; filled into the appended 0s, the frame is 10101101. Receiver's check: 10101101 divided by 10011 leaves remainder 0.

title.en: Why a remainder of 0 means pass
title.zh: 为什么余数为 0 就通过

intro.en: Two questions: why does filling the remainder back in make the frame divisible; and why do flipped bits make the remainder no longer 0. The ⊕ below is XOR, that is, modulo-2 addition and subtraction.
intro.zh: 两个问题：为什么把余数填回去，帧就能被整除；为什么翻转的比特会让余数不再是 0。下面的 ⊕ 是异或，也就是模 2 的加和减。

why.en: Divide the frame padded with r 0s by modulo-2 division to get quotient Q and remainder R (at most r bits). Just like 1000 = 7×142 + 6.
why.zh: 对补了 r 个 0 的帧做模 2 除法，得到商 Q 和余数 R (最多 r 位)。和 1000 = 7×142 + 6 一样。

why.en: Fill the remainder into the low r padded bits. In modulo 2, subtract and add are both XOR, so subtracting the remainder is XORing in the remainder.
why.zh: 把余数填进补 0 的低 r 位。模 2 里减和加都是异或，所以减去余数，就是异或上余数。

why.en: R XOR itself is 0, leaving only Q·G, so T is divisible by G and the remainder is 0.
why.zh: R 异或它自己等于 0，只剩下 Q·G，所以 T 能被 G 整除，余数是 0。

why.en: E is the error pattern: flipped bits are 1, the rest are 0.
why.zh: E 是错误图案：被翻转的位是 1，其余是 0。

lines.tex: (T\oplus E)\bmod G = (T\bmod G)\oplus(E\bmod G) = E\bmod G

why.en: Modulo-2 division distributes over XOR, and T's remainder is 0. So the remainder the receiver sees is the error pattern's own remainder.
why.zh: 模 2 除法对异或是分得开的，而 T 的余数是 0。接收方看到的余数，就是错误图案自己的余数。

why.en: Only if the error pattern happens to be a multiple of G is the remainder coincidentally 0 and the error missed.
why.zh: 只有错误图案恰好是 G 的倍数，余数才碰巧是 0，错误才漏掉。

why.en: A single bit flip: E has just one term x^i, whose factors are all powers of x, and G is not a power of x, so it can't divide it: always detected.
why.zh: 单个比特翻转，E 只有一项 x^i，它的因子都是 x 的幂，而 G 不是 x 的幂，整除不了，一定检出。

why.en: A burst of length at most r: E is x^i times a B of degree less than r. G has degree r, higher than B, and shares no factor with x, so it can't divide it: always detected.
why.zh: 长度不超过 r 的突发：E 是 x^i 乘一个次数小于 r 的 B。G 的次数是 r，比 B 高，又和 x 没有公因子，整除不了，一定检出。

outro.en: So the choice of G decides which errors are detected: a good G is guaranteed to catch every single-bit error and every burst of length at most r. Longer bursts are missed only when the error pattern happens to be a multiple of G (for a burst of length exactly r+1, the pattern must equal G exactly). The standard 32-bit CRC has distance 4, which holds only when the frame is not too long, beyond the slides.
outro.zh: 所以 G 的选择决定能检出哪些错误：好的 G 保证抓住所有单比特错误和所有长度不超过 r 的突发。更长的突发只有在错误图案恰好是 G 的倍数时才漏掉 (长度恰为 r+1 的突发，图案要恰好等于 G)。标准 32 位 CRC 的距离是 4，也只在帧不太长时成立，超出课件。

title.zh: 哪种错误 CRC 看不见

prompt.en: The frame sent is 10101101, and the receiver checks with G = 10011. Which of these errors will CRC certainly fail to detect?
prompt.zh: 发送的帧是 10101101，接收方用 G = 10011 检查。下面哪种错误，CRC 一定检不出？

label.en: Flipping a single bit

feedback.en: The error pattern of a single bit has just one 1, corresponding to $x^i$; G is not a power of x and cannot divide it, so it is always detected.
feedback.zh: 单个比特的错误图案只有一个 1，对应 $x^i$，G 不是 x 的幂，整除不了，一定检出。

label.en: Flipping 4 consecutive bits (burst length 4)
label.zh: 连续翻转 4 位 (突发长度 4)

feedback.en: For a burst no longer than r = 4, the pattern has lower degree than G and can't be a multiple of G, so it is always detected.
feedback.zh: 长度不超过 r = 4 的突发，图案的次数比 G 小，不可能是 G 的倍数，一定检出。

label.en: Over 5 consecutive positions, the flip pattern is exactly 10011 (bits 1, 4 and 5 flipped)
label.zh: 连续 5 个位置上，翻转的图案恰好是 10011 (第 1、4、5 位翻转)

label.en: Flipping any two bits

feedback.en: For this G, two errors would have to be 15 or more bits apart to possibly hit a multiple of G; this frame has only 8 bits, so it is always detected.
feedback.zh: 对这个 G，两位错要相隔 15 位以上才可能碰上 G 的倍数，这一帧只有 8 位，一定检出。

explain.en: The remainder the receiver sees equals the remainder of the error pattern divided by G. The pattern 10011 is G itself, with remainder 0, so such an error is always missed. For example, flip the first 5 bits of 10101101 with this pattern, receive 00110101, divide the whole string by 10011, and the remainder is still 0: it passes. This is also why G has to be chosen carefully: chosen well, none of the common error patterns (single bits, short bursts) is a multiple of G.
explain.zh: 接收方看到的余数，等于错误图案自己除以 G 的余数。图案 10011 就是 G，余数是 0，这样的错误一个也漏掉。例如把 10101101 的前 5 位按这个图案翻转，收到 00110101，整串除以 10011，余数仍是 0，通过。这也是 G 要精心挑选的原因：挑得好，常见的错误图案 (单比特、短突发) 都不会是 G 的倍数。

title.en: How many check bits, and where

text.en: Goal: when only one bit is wrong, not only know there was an error but point to which bit. Each check bit answers a yes/no question (is the parity of certain bits right), and k check bits give $2^k$ combinations of answers. These combinations must say: no error (1 case), or the error is in one of the n+k positions (n+k cases). So:
text.zh: 目标：只错一位时，不但知道出了错，还要指出是哪一位。每个校验位回答一道是非题 (某几位的奇偶对不对)，k 个校验位的答案有 $2^k$ 种组合。这些组合要说清：没出错 (1 种)，或者 n+k 个位置里错在某一个 (n+k 种)。所以：

text.en: 4 data bits: with k = 2, $4 \ge 7$ does not hold; with k = 3, $8 \ge 8$ holds. At least 3 check bits are needed, 7 bits in all.
text.zh: 4 位数据：k = 2 时 $4 \ge 7$ 不成立；k = 3 时 $8 \ge 8$ 成立。至少要 3 个校验位，一共 7 位。

text.en: Positions are numbered from 1. Check bits go at positions that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4), and data at the other positions. The slides call every position P; to avoid confusion, here check bits are called P and data bits D. Write the position number in binary; each bit that is 1 puts the position under that check bit's charge:
text.zh: 位置从 1 开始编号。校验位放在编号是 2 的幂的位置 (1、2、4)，数据放在其余位置。课件把每个位置都叫 P，这里为了不混，校验位叫 P，数据位叫 D。位置编号写成二进制，哪一位是 1，就归哪个校验位管：

text.en: This is what the slides mean by “the position number contains the term p”: P1 covers 1, 3, 5, 7, P2 covers 2, 3, 6, 7, and P4 covers 4, 5, 6, 7. Each check bit makes the number of 1s in the group it covers (itself included) even.
text.zh: 这就是课件说的「位置编号里含 p 项」：P1 管 1、3、5、7，P2 管 2、3、6、7，P4 管 4、5、6、7。每个校验位让它管的那一组 (连它自己) 1 的个数是偶数。

why.en: The data 0101 goes in order into positions 3, 5, 6, 7.
why.zh: 数据 0101 依次放进位置 3、5、6、7。

why.en: P1 covers 1, 3, 5, 7; even parity, so the number of 1s in this group must be even.
why.zh: P1 管 1、3、5、7；偶校验，这一组里 1 的个数要是偶数。

why.en: P2 covers 2, 3, 6, 7.
P4 covers 4, 5, 6, 7.
Arranged in positions 1 to 7, this is the codeword that is sent.
why.zh: 按位置 1 到 7 排好，就是发送的码字。

title.en: Decoding: the failed checks add up to the error position
title.zh: 解码：失败的检查加起来，就是出错的位置

text.en: The receiver checks the parity of each of the three groups, and records the number (1, 2 or 4) of any that fail.
text.zh: 接收方对三组各查一次奇偶，失败的记下它的编号 (1、2 或 4)。

items.en: **Received 0100100** (bit 7 flipped): the P1 group (1, 3, 5, 7) is 0, 0, 1, 0, odd, so it fails; the P2 group (2, 3, 6, 7) is 1, 0, 0, 0, so it fails; the P4 group (4, 5, 6, 7) is 0, 1, 0, 0, so it fails. All three groups fail, $1+2+4=7$, so bit 7 is wrong; flip it back.

**Received 0000101** (bit 2 flipped): the P1 group is 0, 0, 1, 1, even, so it passes; the P2 group is 0, 0, 0, 1, so it fails; the P4 group is 0, 1, 0, 1, so it passes. Only P2 fails, so bit 2 is wrong. This is a check bit itself being wrong; the data is fine.
items.zh: **收到 0000101** (第 2 位翻了)：P1 组 0、0、1、1，偶数，通过；P2 组 0、0、0、1，失败；P4 组 0、1、0、1，通过。只有 P2 失败，第 2 位错。这是校验位自己错了，数据没事。

text.en: Why do the numbers of the failed checks add up to exactly the position? Because the binary form of a position records “which groups cover it”. Position 7 = 111, all three groups cover it, so if it is wrong all three fail; position 2 is covered only by P2, so only P2 fails. It is like binary search: three yes/no questions narrow seven positions down to one.
text.zh: 为什么失败的编号加起来正好是位置？因为位置的二进制写法，记录的就是「它被哪几组管着」。第 7 位 = 111，三组都管它，它错了三组都失败；第 2 位只有 P2 管，只有 P2 失败。像二分查找：三个是非题，把七个位置缩成一个。

body.en: Flip bits 3 and 5 of 0100101 at the same time to get 0110001: the P1 group passes, the P2 group fails, the P4 group fails, $2+4=6$. The receiver will flip bit 6, leaving three bits wrong, and it does not know. The Hamming code has distance 3 and only guarantees to correct one bit.
body.zh: 把 0100101 的第 3、5 位同时翻转，得到 0110001：P1 组通过，P2 组失败，P4 组失败，$2+4=6$。接收方会把第 6 位翻转，结果三位都是错的，而且它不知道。汉明码的距离是 3，只保证纠一位。

prompt.en: An even-parity Hamming code, with check bits at positions 1, 2 and 4. The receiver gets 0011101 and knows only one bit is wrong. Which bit is it?
prompt.zh: 偶校验的汉明码，校验位在位置 1、2、4。接收方收到 0011101，已知只错了一位。错的是第几位？

hints.en: P1 covers 1, 3, 5, 7, P2 covers 2, 3, 6, 7, P4 covers 4, 5, 6, 7.
Which groups have an odd number of 1s? Add up the numbers of the failed ones.
hints.zh: 哪几组 1 的个数是奇数？把失败的编号加起来。

explain.en: Positions 1 to 7 are 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1 in order. P1 group (1, 3, 5, 7): 0, 1, 1, 1, odd, fails. P2 group (2, 3, 6, 7): 0, 1, 0, 1, even, passes. P4 group (4, 5, 6, 7): 1, 1, 0, 1, odd, fails. $1+4=5$, so bit 5 is wrong.

rows.en: 1-bit errors (and any odd number of bits)
3-bit errors, and also bursts of up to 32 bits
rows.zh: 3 位错，另外还能检出长度不超过 32 位的突发错误

text.en: Correction or detection: which pays off? The two have different cost profiles: **correction** spends extra check bits on every frame but never resends; **detection** has fewer check bits per frame, but a frame in error is resent whole. The slides give only the conclusion; here we work it out with a bit error rate. Simple model: each bit is independently wrong with probability p, and a frame holds 1000 data bits.
text.zh: 纠错和检错，哪个划算？两者的开销形状不同：**纠错** 每帧都要多花校验位，但不用重发；**检错** 每帧校验位少，但出错的帧要整帧重发。课件只给了结论，这里用误码率算一遍。简化模型：每个比特独立地以概率 p 出错，帧含 1000 个数据位。

text.en: On the detection side, three steps: the probability the whole frame is error-free; how many sends on average; how many bits the resends waste. Let a frame have L bits in all (1000 data bits plus a 32-bit CRC, L = 1032):
text.zh: 检错这一边，算三步：整帧没出错的概率；平均要发几次；重发白白浪费了多少位。设一帧共 L 位 (1000 个数据位加 32 位 CRC，L = 1032)：

text.en: Take $p=10^{-3}$ as an example:

Add the fixed 32 check bits per frame, and the total is about 1900 bits. The correction side needs no probability: each 11 data bits get 4 check bits ($2^4=16\ge11+4+1$), so 1000 data bits make about 91 blocks, about 364 bits in all, the same whether the line is good or bad.
text.zh: 再加每帧固定的 32 位校验，共约 1900 位。纠错这一边不用算概率：每 11 位数据配 4 位校验 ($2^4=16\ge11+4+1$)，1000 位数据约 91 块，共约 364 位，线路好坏都一样。

rows.en: Fixed extra cost per 1000 data bits
rows.zh: 每 1000 数据位固定多花

rows.en: About 364 bits (4 check bits per 11 data bits, $2^4=16\ge11+4+1$)
Chance a frame is in error about 0.1%, resending wastes about 1 bit, about 33 bits in all
rows.zh: 整帧出错概率约 0.1%，重发浪费约 1 位，共约 33 位

rows.en: Chance a frame is error-free about 0.356, about 2.8 sends on average, about 1870 bits wasted, about 1900 bits in all
rows.zh: 整帧无错的概率约 0.356，平均要发约 2.8 次，浪费约 1870 位，共约 1900 位

text.en: On a good line errors are rare, so detection costs only a few check bits and the fixed overhead of correction isn't worth it. On a noisy line, nearly every frame must be resent whole, and it is better to pay a few more check bits per frame and fix errors on the spot. This is the slides' conclusion: wireless uses correction, high-quality cable uses detection.
text.zh: 好线路几乎不出错，检错只要多付一点校验位，纠错的固定开销就不划算。噪声大的线路，整帧几乎总要重发，不如每帧多付一点校验位把错误当场改掉。这就是课件的结论：无线用纠错，优质线缆用检错。

body.en: Correction first has to assume at most how many errors a frame has, and both data bits and check bits can be wrong. Correction is not foolproof either: at $p=10^{-3}$, about 1% of frames have some block with two errors, which gets corrected wrongly, because a Hamming code only guarantees to fix one bit. The table also leaves out the cost of ACKs, and real errors often come in bursts; it is only meant to make the trade-off clear. The standard 32-bit CRC's distance of 4 also holds only when the frame is not too long, beyond the slides.
body.zh: 纠错要先假设每帧最多出几位错，而且数据位和校验位都可能出错。纠错也不是万无一失：$p=10^{-3}$ 时，约 1% 的帧里某一块会错两位，被改成错的，因为汉明码只保证纠一位。上表也没有计入 ack 的开销，真实的错误常成串，只是为了看清取舍。标准 32 位 CRC 的距离 4，也只在帧不太长时成立，超出课件。

prompt.en: Still a frame of 1000 data bits. A link's bit error rate is $p=10^{-4}$. The detection scheme attaches 32 more check bits (frame length L = 1032) and resends the whole frame on error; the correction scheme gives each 11 data bits 4 check bits. For every 1000 data bits, which scheme spends fewer extra bits?
prompt.zh: 仍是 1000 个数据位的帧。一条链路的误码率 $p=10^{-4}$。检错方案多附 32 位校验 (帧长 L = 1032)，出错整帧重发；纠错方案每 11 位数据配 4 位校验。每 1000 个数据位，哪种方案额外花的比特更少？

label.en: Correction is better, about 364 bits vs about 1900 for detection
label.zh: 纠错更划算，约 364 位 vs 检错约 1900 位

feedback.en: 1900 bits is the figure for $p=10^{-3}$. This line's error rate is ten times lower, so recompute.
feedback.zh: 1900 位是 $p=10^{-3}$ 时的数字。这条线的误码率低十倍，要重新算。

label.en: Detection is better, about 144 bits vs about 364 for correction
label.zh: 检错更划算，约 144 位 vs 纠错约 364 位

label.en: About the same

feedback.en: They differ by more than double. The fixed overhead of correction (about 364 bits) is too big here.
feedback.zh: 差了两倍多。纠错的固定开销 (约 364 位) 在这里太大了。

label.en: Can't compare; you need to know the total frame length
label.zh: 没法比，要知道帧一共多长

feedback.en: The frame length is already given: 1000 data bits.
feedback.zh: 帧长已经给了：1000 数据位。

explain.en: The frame is 1032 bits. The probability the whole frame is error-free is $0.9999^{1032}\approx0.902$, about 1.109 sends on average, wasting about $1032\times0.109\approx112$ bits; with the 32 check bits that is about 144 bits, fewer than correction's 364. At a somewhat higher error rate, the conclusion flips.
explain.zh: 帧长 1032 位。整帧无错的概率是 $0.9999^{1032}\approx0.902$，平均要发约 1.109 次，浪费约 $1032\times0.109\approx112$ 位，加上 32 位校验共约 144 位，比纠错的约 364 位少。误码率再高一些，结论就会翻过来。

text.en: The receiver gets a long string of bits and first has to find the boundaries: character count is simple but one error ruins everything; flag bytes with byte stuffing and start/end flags with bit stuffing find boundaries by markers, and can realign after an error.
text.zh: 接收方拿到一长串比特，先要找到边界：字符计数简单但一错全错；标志字节配字节填充、起止标志配比特填充，则靠记号找边界，错了还能重新对齐。

text.en: Then detect errors: add redundancy. A parity bit is one bit, distance 2, and misses errors in an even number of bits; the Internet checksum adds and complements, and cannot detect reordering; CRC uses polynomial modulo-2 division, fills the remainder back so the whole frame is divisible by G, the receiver divides the whole string again, and a remainder of 0 means pass; flipped bits turn the remainder into the error pattern's own remainder.
text.zh: 再要发现错误：加冗余。奇偶校验一位，距离 2，漏掉偶数位错误；互联网校验和相加取反，调换顺序检不出；CRC 用多项式模 2 除法，把余数填回去让整帧能被 G 整除，接收方整串再除，余数 0 就通过，翻转的比特会让余数变成错误图案自己的余数。

text.en: Finally, fix them: Hamming distance ≥ d+1 to detect d bits, ≥ 2d+1 to correct d bits, and the two cannot both be pushed to the maximum. In a Hamming code the failed checks add up to the error position, and it guarantees to correct only one bit. Detect or correct depends on the line's bit error rate: on a good line, detect and retransmit; on a noisy line, correct directly.
text.zh: 最后是改回来：汉明距离 ≥ d+1 才检出 d 位，≥ 2d+1 才纠正 d 位，两样不能同时开到最大。汉明码让失败的检查加起来就是出错的位置，只保证纠一位。检错还是纠错，看线路的误码率：好线路检错重传，噪声大的线路直接纠错。

text.en: At this point, one frame between two neighbouring machines has boundaries, can be checked for errors, and can be resent. The next lesson asks: when many machines share one wire, whose turn is it to speak?
text.zh: 到这里，相邻两台机器之间的一帧，已经有边界、能查错、能重发。下一课接着问：很多台机器共用同一条线时，轮到谁说话？
